statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F=x\vec i+y\vec j+z\vec k through the surface S, which is a closed cylinder of radius 2, centered on the y-axis, with -5\le y\le 5, and oriented outward.

static.solution: x \vec i + z\vec k contribute to the flux. Since x \vec i + z \vec k is perpendicular to the curved surface and ||x \vec i + z\vec k||=2 there (because the cylinder has radius 2), we have \mbox {Flux through sides} = 2\cdot\mbox{Area of curved surface}= 2\cdot 2\pi\cdot 2\cdot 10 = 80 \pi. On the flat ends, only y\vec j contributes to the flux. On one end, y = 5 and d\vec A=\vec j dA; on the other end, y = -5 and d\vec A = -\vec j dA. Thus \mbox{Flux through ends} = 5\vec j\cdot \vec j\pi(2^2) +(-5\vec j)\cdot (-\vec j\pi(2^2)) = 40 \pi. So, \mbox {Total flux} = 80\pi + 40\pi = 120\pi.
